Legs.Subject: GreatestCommonDivisor<int> at the zero fast paths and the ordinary mixed-sign general path: (other 0, value -3) -> 3, (other -7, value 0) -> 7, (other 8, value -12) -> 4, (other -24, value 54) -> 6
Legs.Against: elementary Euclidean division verified by hand: gcd(3,0)=3, gcd(7,0)=7, gcd(12,8)=4, gcd(54,24)=6 -- a different algorithm and a different derivation route from the subject's Stein binary descent, sharing no line and no idea with it

Legs.Subject: the two near-signed-minimum branches the member's own documentation describes: exactly one operand at int.MinValue returns the other operand's own highest power-of-two factor -- (other 1, value int.MinValue) -> 1 and (other 12, value int.MinValue) -> 4 -- and BOTH operands at int.MinValue throws OverflowException naming the unrepresentable magnitude, exactly as the member's <exception> doc states. This is the documented shortcut and its documented refusal, checked directly rather than against a second GCD algorithm that would only restate the same reasoning
LeastCommonMultiple<int> over representable operands: (other 6, value 4) -> 12, (other 5, value 0) -> 0, (other 6, value -4) -> 12, (other -6, value 4) -> 12
Legs.Against: elementary arithmetic verified by hand -- lcm(a,b) = |a*b| / gcd(a,b), with lcm(n,0) conventionally zero -- independent of the subject's divide-before-multiply order and its sign-of-the-operands correction

Legs.Subject: the documented overflow contract at (other 2, value int.MaxValue) -> -2 and (other 2, value -int.MaxValue) -> -2: the true product 2*(2^31-1) exceeds int and the member's own doc says the result WRAPS rather than throws, and that the sign correction reads the pre-multiplication operand signs rather than the wrapped product's sign -- no finite oracle decides a value the carrier cannot hold, so this states the carrier's own declared contract directly, matching its documentation rather than diverging from it

EnumerateDigits, LogarithmBase10, LeastSignificantDigit, MostSignificantDigit and DigitalRoot at int.MinValue, whose magnitude 2147483648 = 2^31 is not representable in int and so is the one operand each member's XML doc calls out as the reason it abs-es a remainder or a quotient rather than the whole value
Legs.Against: the decimal expansion of 2^31 = 2,147,483,648 worked out on paper: ten digits, least-significant-first [8,4,6,3,8,4,7,4,1,2], leading digit 2, ones digit 8, and a digit sum 2+1+4+7+4+8+3+6+4+8=47 reducing to 4+7=11 to 1+1=2 -- arithmetic on the literal, independent of and prior to any of the subject's DivRem or modulo-nine-residue implementations

Legs.Subject: Exponentiate<int> rejects a negative exponent with ArgumentOutOfRangeException, exactly as its own doc requires ('must be non-negative, since a negative integer power is not representable'), asserted at exponent -1.
